items.html:
Implemented default precision support.

  • JAX accepts float32/complex64, works with default x64 disabled, and keeps native computation in double precision. Outputs follow JAX’s precision setting; gradients retain input dtype.
  • PyTorch accepts float32/complex64, returns native double-precision outputs, and preserves input-gradient dtype.
  • Shared conversion helpers validate before native coercion. Existing CPU and first-order limits remain.

Verified 61 tests, Ruff, Pyrefly, and fresh-process ordinary API examples without backend imports, including JAX eager/JIT. Also checked oblique incidence and slab JIT.

Changed only jax.py, torch.py, _records.py, and their three assigned test files. Notified documentation and shared-test owners about the revised contract. No commits or builds.
